Consequently, relying on tool outputs for 'before/after' comparisons led to uncertainty. The correct clinical interpretation required recognizing that while the mass decreased significantly, leading to left lower lobe re-expansion and reduced mediastinal shift, it did not necessarily resolve completely in the specific timeframe or manner suggested by the 'complete resolution' option. While initial reasoning suggested displacement of the heart and trachea, the correct observation was that the mass caused compression of the right lung without significant tracheal or cardiac displacement. Post-surgical imaging confirmed re-expansion of the right lung while the heart and trachea remained in their original positions. This case illustrates that large posterior masses may compress adjacent lung parenchyma without shifting midline structures, a finding that contradicts the assumption that all significant mediastinal masses cause tracheal deviation. Limitations noted include the inability of single-image AI tools to establish chronology or detect subtle interval changes without explicit timepoint binding."]
